title: AgentRun computer protocol 0.2: methods
$comment: Generated from packages/computer/src/protocol.ts (DaemonMethods) by node scripts/generate-computer-spec.mjs. Each property of DaemonMethods is a method: its params and its result.

path.description: A file already in the computer (files.write first).
path.title: path

id.description: A bundle id or a package name: "com.apple.Notes", "com.android.settings".
id.title: id

url.description: Open this in the app: a deep link, or a page in a browser.
url.title: url

background.description: Open it without bringing it to the front (feature apps.background). Without the feature, refused as `unsupported`.
background.title: background

foreground.description: The id of the app in front, or null.
foreground.title: foreground

ComputerKind.description: What a computer is (its machine kind): the shape its tools take. Kind sets which groups are Core.
ComputerKind.title: ComputerKind

ComputerOs.description: The platform a computer runs, which the key table and exec need.
ComputerOs.title: ComputerOs

DaemonErrorKind.description: error.data.kind in the daemon's error replies.
DaemonErrorKind.title: DaemonErrorKind

DaemonMethods.description: Every method the daemon answers: its params and its result.

DeadlineExtendParams.description: Moves init's own deadline. Init refuses an earlier one. Typed now; the daemon answers it from the X11 shim's PR on.
DeadlineExtendParams.title: DeadlineExtendParams

at.description: The deadline init holds after the call, ISO time.
at.title: at

argv.description: The program and its arguments. Never a shell: a shell is the caller's choice (["sh", "-c", "..."]).
argv.title: argv

cwd.description: Absolute, or relative to the user's home. Default: the daemon's working directory.
cwd.title: cwd

env.description: Added over a minimal default (PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME); nothing else of the daemon's environment is passed.
env.title: env

user.description: A user name, or uid[:gid]. A daemon that cannot switch users answers `denied`.
user.title: user

maxOutput.description: Bytes kept of each stream; default and most MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES.
maxOutput.title: maxOutput

exitCode.description: null when a signal ended the program.
exitCode.title: exitCode

signal.description: The signal that ended it, without SIG, such as "KILL".
signal.title: signal

FeatureOff.description: A feature that is off, and why: "Screen Recording is not granted to Computerd".
FeatureOff.title: FeatureOff

mode.description: The permission bits, with setuid, setgid and sticky: 0o7777.
mode.title: mode

mode.description: The permission bits, with setuid, setgid and sticky: 0o7777.
mode.title: mode

path.description: A directory; a symlink to one is followed. Symlinks below it are listed, never entered.
path.title: path

offset.description: Skip this many entries: pass the count already read to get the next page.
offset.title: offset

entries.description: In walk order: each directory's entries by name, a directory before what it holds.
entries.title: entries

truncated.description: More entries follow: list again with offset + entries.length.
truncated.title: truncated

parents.description: Make missing parents, and accept a directory already there.
parents.title: parents

overwrite.description: Replace what is at `to`, as rename(2) does: a file, or an empty directory.
overwrite.title: overwrite

FilesReadParams.description: Paths are absolute; the daemon cleans them. A relative path is `invalid`.
FilesReadParams.title: FilesReadParams

length.description: Default and most MAX_CHUNK_BYTES; more is refused as `limit`.
length.title: length

size.description: The file's size when it was read.
size.title: size

recursive.description: Remove a directory and everything in it. A symlink is removed, never followed.
recursive.title: recursive

follow.description: Follow a symlink at path. Default false: a symlink is reported as one.
follow.title: follow

data.description: base64; the request line holds at most 1 MiB.
data.title: data

offset.description: Write here without truncating. With neither offset nor append, the file is replaced.
offset.title: offset

mode.description: Set when given (0o7777 bits), else 0o644 for a new file.
mode.title: mode

Group.description:
What a computer offers, as one flat list: capabilities().groups, repeated in hello.groups. A sub-flag such as
input.touch is its own entry. Each is optional unless kind makes it Core. cdp, stream and downloads are the
provider's, not computerd's: cdp a browser's CDP target (ComputerConnection.cdp), stream a live view of the screen
(provider.stream()), downloads the files a browser saved; a daemon's hello never lists them.
Group.title: Group

client.description: Who is asking, for the daemon's log: a name and version.
client.title: client

protocol.description: The protocol version this computer speaks: PROTOCOL_VERSION.
protocol.title: protocol

version.description: The daemon's own version (with daemon none, the provider's).
version.title: version

osVersion.description:
The OS's own version as the computer says it: a phone's Android release (getprop ro.build.version.release), such
as "15". Absent where the computer does not say one.
osVersion.title: osVersion

arch.description: Go's name for the architecture: amd64, arm64.
arch.title: arch

display.description: The DISPLAY a desktop's screen and input methods drive, such as ":99"; absent on any other computer.
display.title: display

fence.description: How init holds its programs off the computer's network, when it gave them one of their own (init --own-network).
fence.title: fence

screen.description: The main screen, in points. Absent on a computer with no screen.
screen.title: screen

features.description:
What this computer's groups can and cannot do here, by the names in FEATURES. A feature that is off says why, in
words a person can act on. A feature not listed is not offered. A caller ignores a name it does not know.
features.title: features

failed.description: The action that failed, and why; absent when every action ran.
failed.title: failed

MountSyncResult.description:
mount.sync: asks the computer's resident Archil sync server (its socket, ARCHIL_SYNC_SOCKET) for one sync of
/workspace, coalesced with any in flight, and answers its exit code: 0 is every write so far durable. A computer with
no Archil mount has no server: not_found.
MountSyncResult.title: MountSyncResult

exitCode.description: null while running, or when a signal ended it.
exitCode.title: exitCode

signal.description: The signal that ended it, without SIG: "TERM", "KILL".
signal.title: signal

argvClipped.description: argv was cut to its first arguments to keep the listing small.
argvClipped.title: argvClipped

exitCode.description: null while running, or when a signal ended it.
exitCode.title: exitCode

signal.description: The signal that ended it, without SIG: "TERM", "KILL".
signal.title: signal

from.description: Where the page starts: the page before's next, or 0 (the default) for the first page.
from.title: from

truncated.description: More follow: list again with from: next.
truncated.title: truncated

next.description: Where the page after this one starts. A process dropped from the table between pages moves no other past it.
next.title: next

stream.description: "stdout" or "stderr"; "pty" for a process started with one; "log" for one started with a log.
stream.title: stream

offset.description: Bytes since the process started. Pass the last read's nextOffset.
offset.title: offset

maxBytes.description: Default and most MAX_CHUNK_BYTES; more is refused as `limit`.
maxBytes.title: maxBytes

waitMs.description: When nothing past offset is there yet, wait up to this long (most MAX_READ_WAIT_MS) for bytes or the end.
waitMs.title: waitMs

dropped.description:
Bytes before offset the ring no longer held: the read began at the ring's start instead. Once an ended process's
ring is let go, every byte from offset on.
dropped.title: dropped

exited.description: The process has ended and nothing is left past nextOffset.
exited.title: exited

size.description: The stream's bytes so far: every byte since the process started, kept in the ring or dropped. For "log", the log's.
size.title: size

capped.description: "log" only: output came past the log's PROCESS_LOG_BYTES and was not written to it.
capped.title: capped

logError.description:
"log" only: a write to the log failed or wrote short (a full disk), so the log stopped there for good and holds
only the output before it: why. Nothing after it is written, so the file stays a true prefix.
logError.title: logError

signal.description:
INT to a process started with a pty is ^C: it goes to the terminal's foreground process group (the job a shell
runs in the foreground, or the program when it runs none), and is refused as denied when that group is outside
the program's session. Every other signal, and INT without a pty, goes to the program's process group. A signal
to a process that has ended does nothing.
signal.title: signal

note.description:
Set only for INT on a terminal: when it found no foreground group (the program let go of it, or is ending) and went
to the program's own group, or when the foreground group had no process left in the program's session by the time
the guard came to signal it (it ended, and its id may have gone to a group in another session) and INT was not
sent: why.
note.title: note

argv.description: The program and its arguments, never a shell string.
argv.title: argv

env.description: Added over the same minimal default as exec.run's.
env.title: env

pty.description: Run in a terminal of this size: one "pty" stream, and the program's own session with it as the controlling terminal.
pty.title: pty

stdin.description: Keep stdin open for process.write. Without it (and without a pty), stdin is /dev/null.
stdin.title: stdin

log.description:
An absolute path for a new file the daemon writes the first PROCESS_LOG_BYTES of the output to, stdout and stderr
(or the terminal's) as they come, and read as the "log" stream. The daemon makes the missing directories and the
file itself (mode 0644, its own); a link at the path or at any directory on its way is refused as `denied`, a
file already there as `exists`, and nothing is started.
log.title: log

waitGroup.description:
The process runs until its program and every process left in its process group (with a pty, its session) have
ended, and reports the program's own exit. A signal goes to what is left of the group once the program is gone.
waitGroup.title: waitGroup

orphans.description: "keep": when the process ends, what it started outside it runs on, to the computer's end, instead of being ended.
orphans.title: orphans

id.description: The daemon's name for the process, such as "p1".
id.title: id

pid.description: The program's pid in the computer.
pid.title: pid

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the end, up to a day; 0 asks without waiting. On timeout, running is true.
timeoutMs.title: timeoutMs

data.description: base64, to stdin or the terminal.
data.title: data

close.description: Close stdin after the data. A terminal has no stdin to close: send "\x04" or signal HUP.
close.title: close

ScreenReadParams.description: One shot is held; it is dropped at eof or at the next shot.
ScreenReadParams.title: ScreenReadParams

region.description: Only this part of the screen; its coordinates stay those of the full screenshot.
region.title: region

size.description:
The PNG's bytes; data holds at most MAX_CHUNK_BYTES of it. The PNG is 8-bit and non-interlaced (gray, RGB, palette,
gray and alpha, or RGBA), as the conformance suite decodes it.
size.title: size

data.description: base64; read the rest with screen.read.
data.title: data

width.description: The image's pixels: the input coordinate space (never downscaled).
width.title: width

scale.description: Device pixels per logical point: 1 on Xvfb; a phone reports its own.
scale.title: scale

cursor.description: Where the pointer is, with input.pointer.
cursor.title: cursor

ScreenSize.description: A screen's size in points, and how many pixels a point holds (2 on a Retina Mac, 2.625 on many phones, 1 on Xvfb).
ScreenSize.title: ScreenSize

ScreenWatchParams.description:
The live view's frames (screen.watch): the next frame after the caller's ack, once the screen changed. `after` is
the seq of the last frame the caller has whole, 0 for none; an older one gets the newest frame at once.
ScreenWatchParams.title: ScreenWatchParams

waitMs.description: The longest wait for a change, in ms, 0 to 10000; default 2000.
waitMs.title: waitMs

maxWidth.description: The frame's width at most (scaled down, never up); default 1280.
maxWidth.title: maxWidth

ScreenWatchResult.description:
changed false: no change within waitMs, and no frame. A frame carries its bytes as screen.shot carries its PNG: the
first MAX_CHUNK_BYTES in data, the rest through screen.read by id.
ScreenWatchResult.title: ScreenWatchResult

format.description: jpeg from computerd; png from a phone client that encodes its own frames.
format.title: format

width.description: The screen's pixels: the input coordinate space.
width.title: width

cursor.description:
In screen and input, pixels of the full screenshot, origin top left (a region shot never changes this space). In ui,
the window's points, origin at its top left.
cursor.title: cursor

path.description: A file (one entry, its name) or a directory (entries relative to it).
path.title: path

id.description: Ending a pull that is not open is fine.
id.title: id

maxBytes.description: Default and most MAX_CHUNK_BYTES; more is refused as `limit`.
maxBytes.title: maxBytes

data.description: base64: maxBytes of the archive, fewer only at its end.
data.title: data

path.description: The directory to extract into; made, with its parents, when missing.
path.title: path

data.description: base64. Send the next write after this one's reply: writes are extracted in the order they arrive.
data.title: data

target.description: Where keys and typing without a ref go. Default: the state's app and window, else the app in front.
target.title: target

state.description: The state the steps' points were read from. A step at a point needs it.
state.title: state

steps.description: At most MAX_STEPS; their drag ms add up to at most MAX_BATCH_WAIT_MS. No steps and an expect is a wait.
steps.title: steps

expect.description:
What the caller expects to see once the steps ran, checked on the computer against the whole window, polled until
it holds or timeoutMs passes. text: some node's name or value holds it. ref: the element exists. Both: that element's
name or value holds the text. gone: the opposite of each. At least one of text and ref.
expect.title: expect

foreground.description: Let steps take the foreground route, which moves the user's pointer and focus. Default false.
foreground.title: foreground

steps.description: One per step tried, in order. A refused step is the last: the steps after it do not run.
steps.title: steps

state.description: The state after the steps, once the window settled (at most MAX_SETTLE_MS).
state.title: state

changed.description: The window's nodes or image changed between before the first step and the settled state.
changed.title: changed

expect.description: Whether the expect held in time. Absent with no expect, or when a step was refused.
expect.title: expect

UiExpect.description:
What the caller expects to see once the steps ran, checked on the computer against the whole window, polled until
it holds or timeoutMs passes. text: some node's name or value holds it. ref: the element exists. Both: that element's
name or value holds the text. gone: the opposite of each. At least one of text and ref.
UiExpect.title: UiExpect

ref.description:
A driver's name for one element, such as "@e12". It stays good while its element exists, across states and steps;
once the element is gone, a step naming it is refused as `stale`. Refs are opaque and start with "@".
ref.title: ref

UiImage.description: A window's image, whole: at most MAX_CHUNK_BYTES before base64 (the driver lowers JPEG quality until it fits).
UiImage.title: UiImage

width.description: Pixels. The image covers the window: a pixel is window.bounds' width / width points.
width.title: width

ref.description:
A driver's name for one element, such as "@e12". It stays good while its element exists, across states and steps;
once the element is gone, a step naming it is refused as `stale`. Refs are opaque and start with "@".
ref.title: ref

name.description: What a person reads it as: its label, title or text.
name.title: name

value.description: What it holds: a text field's text, a slider's value. A secure field's value is never sent.
value.title: value

id.description: The app's own name for it, when it has one: an Android resource-id, a macOS accessibility identifier.
id.title: id

parent.description: The nearest node above it in this list; absent at the top. A node comes after its parent.
parent.title: parent

actions.description: The platform's own action names, for the perform step: "AXShowMenu", "ACTION_LONG_CLICK".
actions.title: actions

target.description: Which app and window. A bundle id or package name, and a window id from ui.observe. Omitted: the app in front, its main window.
target.title: target

full.description: Every node. Without it, only the nodes that can be acted on or that have a name, and their parents.
full.title: full

image.description: The window's image (feature ui.image), true at DEFAULT_IMAGE_EDGE. Without the feature, refused as `unsupported`.
image.title: image

since.description: A state this connection observed before: the result says what changed since it.
since.title: since

state.description: This observation's id, such as "s7". A step's points are read against the state they came from.
state.title: state

window.description: bounds in screen points: where the window sits.
window.title: window

nodes.description: In order, a node after its parent.
nodes.title: nodes

diff.description: Against since, by ref. Absent when since was not given or the driver no longer holds it.
diff.title: diff

image.description: A window's image, whole: at most MAX_CHUNK_BYTES before base64 (the driver lowers JPEG quality until it fits).
image.title: image

truncated.description: Nodes were left out: past MAX_UI_NODES, or to keep the reply within the line limit.
truncated.title: truncated

UiRoute.description: The ways a driver can make a step happen, best first. A step's result says which one ran.
UiRoute.title: UiRoute

UiStep.description:
One action. A step that names a ref acts on its element; a step at a point needs the act's state, and is refused as
`stale` when what is under the point is no longer what that state saw.
UiStep.title: UiStep

press.description:
A driver's name for one element, such as "@e12". It stays good while its element exists, across states and steps;
once the element is gone, a step naming it is refused as `stale`. Refs are opaque and start with "@".
press.title: press
